Tuned Lamborghini Urus in Verde Turbine and Dry Carbon Is Something Else Indeed
13 photos
Photo: Instagram | lartedesign
Even though it is far from being a fresh product anymore, the Lamborghini Urus still makes headlines after all these years. And believe us when we say this, the Italian company’s exotic crossover has started to show its age.
That’s because production started all the way back in 2017 at the Sant’Agata Bolognese facility in Italy (where else?), and five years later, the automaker retired the original Urus, replacing it with the facelifted iteration. The lineup was also expanded to include two members, the Urus Performante and the Urus S, both getting revised looks, some mods beneath the skin, and a power boost from 641 hp (650 ps/478 kW) to 657 hp (666 ps/490 kW).
As you likely recall, the former was a more track-focused version, and was a couple of tenths of a second faster than the latter, despite the fact that both featured the same powertrain in the same configuration. The Raging Bull then expanded the lineup with the Urus SE , the first-ever plug-in hybrid version of the high-riding model. The electrified 4.0-liter twin-turbocharged V8 engine was officially rated at 789 hp (800 ps/589 kW) and 710 lb-ft (950 Nm) of torque, and 0-62 mph (100 kph) took 3.4 seconds.
But why do we speak about this model in past tense when it came out two years ago? Because that’s how long it lived before the automaker pulled the plug on it. The sole surviving member of the Urus lineup is the new Urus SE Performante. This model has dropped the sprint time to 3.3 seconds, identical to yesterday’s non-electrified Performante, and has 801 hp (812 ps/597 kW) and 738 lb-ft (1,000 Nm) of torque in total available via the right pedal, produced by its upgraded PHEV powertrain.
Photo: Instagram | lartedesign Now, the Lamborghini Urus SE may be dead and buried, but it is the model that has started getting the most coverage in our news feed. That’s because quite a few tuners have dropped all kinds of modded takes on it these past few weeks and months, and Larte Design’s name is definitely toward the top of the list. One of their latest projects based on this model can be seen in the photo gallery, and it definitely looks quite memorable, especially if you are into tuned examples.
In our (or my, in this case) opinion, one of the first things that makes it stand out from a crowd is the Verde Turbine matte paint finish, and the exposed dry carbon elements. The former is the color that dominates the entire exterior of this tuned Lamborghini Urus SE, and the latter can be seen on some of the add-ons. The latter include the new splitter with blades on the sides, the fresh side skirts, the wheels arch trim, and some extras in the front bumper.
This modded Italian exotic crossover also benefits from a quite large diffuser at the rear, which features the ever-present extra brake light. Or two of them, in this case. The tailpipe trim appears to be new as well, and further up, it sports a ducktail spoiler above the taillights, as well as a new roof-mounted wing. Are the Y-spoke alloys, shod in Pirelli P Zero tires, part of the makeover, too? Your guess is as good as ours, and since we’re not exactly wheel experts, we will leave this answer to you.
Photo: Instagram | lartedesign Do you want to see the interior of this modded Lamborghini Urus SE? Well, so do we, but unfortunately, Larte Design hasn’t released any images of it at the time of writing. And you know what this usually means, don’t you? With an emphasis on the word “usually,” that would be that the vehicle in question probably retains its stock upholstery, trim, and so on.
There is also no word on power, and chances are that this machine might not offer any more oomph, and that would be all right, as the model is already very punchy with no mods.
There is no detail on the pricing part of the extras mentioned above either, which fit the 2025 to 2027 model year Lamborghini Urus SE , though the money part shouldn’t be an issue to owners, given that a used Urus SE tends to retail from $270,000 to over $350,000 in today’s used car market in the United States of America, based on the model year, mileage, options, and overall appearance.
Nevertheless, Larte Design invites interested parties to reach out to them and discuss the details, so your Lamborghini Urus SE could also look like this. But the question is, would you want it to? If you said yes, and you have a Urus SE parked in your garage, then congrats, and you may want to contact the tuner for the next part. Before wrapping it up and moving on to the next topic, let us know if you fancy the look of this tuned example by dropping a few lines below.
